config.title: Component Library Theming

intro.title: Component Library Theming
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple themed button component library using React and TypeScript. You'll learn how to use React Context to manage and apply a consistent theme—like colors and fonts—across multiple components. The main technologies involved are React's Context API for state management and TypeScript interfaces for defining theme types. By the end, you'll understand how to create a reusable theming system that keeps your UI components looking uniform and easy to customize.
intro.usecase: Component library theming is essential for building consistent, brand-aligned user interfaces across large-scale applications. For example, a SaaS dashboard might use a dark theme for data visualization panels while offering a light theme for content-heavy admin sections, all using the same underlying component library. Developers implement theming to allow users to toggle between themes in settings menus, or to apply contextual themes to different parts of an app like modals and sidebars. This pattern is foundational in design systems used by companies like Shopify or Airbnb to maintain visual coherence while enabling customization.

objectives: Implement a theme provider component to distribute theme values throughout a React application
Configure theme tokens for consistent color, typography, and spacing values
Apply theme values to component styles using custom hooks or context consumption
Construct themed UI components that adapt to different theme configurations
Update component variants to respond to theme changes dynamically
Integrate a theme switching mechanism to toggle between light and dark modes
Manipulate theme objects to extend or override default design system values

steps.title: Import React and createTheme from @mui/material
steps.instruction: Import React and createTheme from '@mui/material' to enable Material-UI theming capabilities.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the createTheme function from the Material-UI library.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and createTheme from '@mui/material' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added, making React and createTheme available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and createTheme are imported from 'react' and '@mui/material' respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but ensure you've imported both React and createTheme from the correct packages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import React from 'react' and createTheme from '@mui/material'.

steps.title: Create a theme configuration object
steps.instruction: Create a theme configuration object named 'theme' using the imported createTheme function. Define primary and secondary color palettes with main colors of your choice.
steps.hint: Call createTheme() with an object containing a palette property that has primary and secondary objects with main color values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A theme object is created with primary and secondary color palettes defined.
successCriteria: A theme object is created using createTheme with primary and secondary color palettes containing main colors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a theme object, but make sure it includes both primary and secondary color palettes with main colors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The theme configuration object wasn't created correctly. Use createTheme with an object containing palette.primary and palette.secondary properties.

steps.title: Import ThemeProvider from @mui/material
steps.instruction: Add an import statement for ThemeProvider from '@mui/material'.
steps.hint: Use the same import syntax you used for createTheme, but specify ThemeProvider instead.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing a component
import { Button } from '@mui/material';
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component is imported and available to use in your code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing ThemeProvider from '@mui/material' using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import ThemeProvider from '@mui/material'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Define a functional component named App that returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure the component name matches exactly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns null, ready to be enhanced in later steps.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a component named App that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a component named App that returns null.

steps.title: Wrap the app with ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, return a ThemeProvider component with the theme prop set to your theme object.
steps.hint: The ThemeProvider should wrap any content you plan to add later. For now, you can return it with an empty fragment or placeholder.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns a ThemeProvider component that wraps the app content, making the theme available to all child components.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider has theme prop set to the theme object
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure ThemeProvider is returned from App and receives the theme object as a prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component should return ThemeProvider with the theme prop set to your theme object. Check your return statement and prop assignment.

steps.title: Import Button and Typography from @mui/material
steps.instruction: Import the Button and Typography components from '@mui/material' to use themed Material-UI components in your app.
steps.hint: Add the imports to the existing import statements at the top of your file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple components from a library
import { Button, Card } from '@mui/material';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button and Typography components are imported and ready to be used inside your App component.
successCriteria: Button and Typography are imported from '@mui/material'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both Button and Typography from '@mui/material'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing Button and Typography from the correct package '@mui/material'.

steps.title: Add a container div inside ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider wrapper in your App component, add a div element with padding and margin styles to serve as a layout container.
steps.hint: Add a div with inline styles like style={{ padding: '20px', margin: '0 auto' }} inside the ThemeProvider tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns a ThemeProvider wrapping a div with padding and margin styles.
successCriteria: A div element with inline styles for padding and margin is added inside the ThemeProvider.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a div, but make sure it has inline styles for padding and margin (e.g., style={{ padding: '20px', margin: '0 auto' }}).
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeProvider should contain a div with padding and margin styles. Check that you've added the div inside the ThemeProvider tags with inline styles.

steps.title: Add a Typography component with primary color
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add a Typography component with variant 'h4' and color 'primary'. Use the text 'Welcome to Themed App'.
steps.hint: The Typography component accepts variant and color props. Use variant='h4' and color='primary'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a styled Typography component
<Typography variant="h4" color="primary">
  Welcome to Themed App
</Typography>
steps.expectedOutcome: A large heading with the primary theme color appears in the container.
successCriteria: Typography component is added with variant h4, color primary, and text 'Welcome to Themed App'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a Typography component, but check that it has variant='h4', color='primary', and the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Typography component is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add it inside the container div with the specified props.

steps.title: Add a Button with primary variant
steps.instruction: Inside the div, after the Typography component, add a Button component with variant='contained' and color='primary'. Include the text 'Primary Button' as its children.
steps.hint: Use the Button component imported from @mui/material. Set the variant and color props as specified.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Adding a themed button
<Button variant="contained" color="primary">Click Me</Button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A primary contained button appears below the Typography, styled according to the theme's primary color.
successCriteria: Button component is added with variant='contained', color='primary', and displays 'Primary Button' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a Button, but check that it has variant='contained', color='primary', and the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component is missing or has incorrect props. Make sure to add it with variant='contained' and color='primary'.

steps.title: Add a secondary Button for contrast
steps.instruction: Add a second Button component below the existing Typography with the variant set to 'outlined' and color set to 'secondary'.
steps.hint: Use the Button component imported from @mui/material with the variant and color props.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a secondary button
<Button variant="outlined" color="secondary">Secondary Action</Button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A secondary outlined button appears below the primary-colored typography, demonstrating the secondary theme color usage.
successCriteria: A Button component with variant='outlined' and color='secondary' is added inside the div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check if it has both variant='outlined' and color='secondary' props to match the theme configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The secondary button wasn't added correctly. Make sure to add a Button component with the outlined variant and secondary color inside the div.
